about.ex: The trip takes about an hour.

according.ex: According to the report, prices fell last year.

accumulate.en: to gradually get more and more of something
accumulate.ex: Dust will accumulate if you never clean.

example.en: Plastic waste continues to accumulate in the oceans.
example.zh: 塑膠垃圾持續在海洋中累積。

note.usage: 可作及物或不及物動詞；常與 debt、data、waste、wealth 搭配；名詞為 accumulation。

noteEn.meaning: to slowly collect or build up over time.
noteEn.usage: Common with waste, debt and wealth; the noun is accumulation.

noteEs.exampleTr: Los residuos plásticos siguen acumulándose en los océanos.
noteEs.meaning: juntar o reunirse poco a poco.
noteEs.usage: Puede llevar objeto o no; va con debt, waste, wealth. Sustantivo: accumulation.

noteHi.exampleTr: प्लास्टिक कचरा समुद्रों में जमा होता जा रहा है।
noteHi.usage: सकर्मक और अकर्मक दोनों; debt, waste, wealth के साथ आम। संज्ञा accumulation।

noteJa.exampleTr: プラスチックごみは海にたまり続けている。
noteJa.meaning: 少しずつたまる、ためる。
noteJa.usage: 自動詞・他動詞の両方。debt, waste, wealth などと結びつく。名詞は accumulation。

noteKo.exampleTr: 플라스틱 쓰레기가 바다에 계속 쌓이고 있다.
noteKo.usage: 자동사·타동사 모두 가능. debt, waste, wealth와 자주 쓴다. 명사는 accumulation.

achieved.ex: The team achieved its sales target in May.

action.en: steps taken to deal with a problem
action.ex: The city needs an action plan for floods.

address.ex: The council must address the housing shortage.

agencies.en: government organisations with a special job
agencies.ex: Two state agencies run the project.

alternative.en: another thing you can use instead
alternative.ex: Cycling is a cheap alternative to driving.

annually.ex: The festival is held annually in May.

approximately.ex: The journey takes approximately two hours.

are.en: form of 'be'; also used in the passive

argues.en: says something is true and gives reasons
argues.ex: She argues that taxes should be lower.

arises.ex: A problem arises when two people want the same room.

around.ex: Around fifty people came to the meeting.

as.en: in the role of; at the time when

asks.ex: Mum asks me to tidy my room every day.

assertion.en: a strong statement that something is true
assertion.ex: His assertion that the bridge was safe was wrong.

at.en: used to show a place, event or point

away.en: (throw away) get rid of as rubbish

back.en: to the place it came from
back.ex: Please put the book back on the shelf.

ballymaloe.ja: バリーマロー（アイルランドの食品ブランド）

be.en: exist or have a quality; used to form the passive
be.ex: The shop will be open tomorrow.

become.ex: The empty lot will become a playground.

being.en: form of 'be' used in the passive after a preposition
being.ex: He hates being told what to do.

big.ex: Moving abroad is a big decision.

bodies.ex: Several public bodies support the plan.

businesses.en: companies that sell goods or services
businesses.ex: Many local businesses closed during the storm.

buyers.en: people or companies that buy goods

calls.en: (calls on) formally asks someone to do something
calls.ex: The mayor calls on drivers to slow down.

came.en: happened or were made (at a certain time)
came.ex: The news came as a big surprise.
came.ja: 出された；（〜の時に）なされた
came.zh: 出現；發表（言論在…時發表）

cent.ex: Prices rose by five per cent last year.

chain.en: a connected series of stages (supply chain)
chain.ex: A delay at the port affected the whole chain.
chain.ja: チェーン（supply chain：サプライチェーン）

champion.en: to publicly support and fight for something
champion.ex: She has always championed the rights of workers.

charities.en: organisations that help people in need

charity.en: an organisation that helps people in need
charity.ex: She gives money to a children's charity.

choice.en: a decision between options; an option
choice.ex: You have a choice of tea or coffee.
choice.zh: 選擇（no choice but to：不得不）

circumstances.en: the facts or conditions of a situation
circumstances.ex: In these circumstances, the trip was cancelled.

claiming.ex: He is claiming that the shop sold him a broken phone.

climate.en: the usual weather patterns of the earth
climate.ex: The climate here is warm and dry.

coincided.en: happened at the same time as something else
coincided.ex: Her birthday coincided with the school holiday.
coincided.ja: 同時に起きた；重なった

example.en: The sale coincided with the start of the holidays.
example.zh: 特賣活動恰逢假期開始。

note.meaning: 同時發生、恰好碰在一起。
note.usage: 常用 coincide with + 事件；名詞 coincidence 是「巧合」。

noteEn.meaning: to happen at the same time as something else.

noteEs.exampleTr: Las rebajas coincidieron con el inicio de las vacaciones.
noteEs.usage: Se usa coincide with + evento; el sustantivo es coincidence.

noteHi.exampleTr: सेल छुट्टियों की शुरुआत के साथ ही हुई।
noteHi.usage: coincide with + घटना के रूप में प्रयोग; संज्ञा coincidence।

noteJa.exampleTr: セールは休暇の始まりと重なった。
noteJa.usage: coincide with + 出来事の形で使う。名詞は coincidence。

noteKo.usage: coincide with + 사건 형태로 쓴다. 명사는 coincidence.

collaborate.ex: The two schools collaborate on science projects.

comments.en: things someone says about a topic
comments.ex: His comments about the food upset the chef.

companies.en: businesses that make or sell things
companies.ex: Many companies let staff work from home.

consequently.ex: It rained heavily; consequently, the match was cancelled.

considerable.ex: The change saved a considerable amount of money.

consumption.en: the act of eating, drinking or using something
consumption.ex: Water consumption rises in hot weather.

example.en: This meat is not fit for human consumption.
example.zh: 這塊肉不適合人類食用。

note.meaning: 食用、飲用或消耗的行為或數量。
note.usage: fit/unfit for human consumption 表示「適合／不適合食用」；動詞為 consume。

noteEn.meaning: the eating, drinking or using of something.
noteEn.usage: fit for consumption = safe to eat; the verb is consume.

noteEs.exampleTr: Esta carne no es apta para el consumo humano.
noteEs.meaning: acción o cantidad de comer, beber o usar algo.
noteEs.usage: fit for human consumption = apto para el consumo; el verbo es consume.

noteHi.exampleTr: यह मांस इंसानों के खाने योग्य नहीं है।
noteHi.meaning: खाने, पीने या उपयोग करने की क्रिया या मात्रा।
noteHi.usage: fit for human consumption = खाने योग्य; क्रिया consume।

noteJa.exampleTr: この肉は人間の食用に適さない。
noteJa.meaning: 食べたり使ったりすること、またその量。
noteJa.usage: fit for human consumption で「食用に適した」。動詞は consume。

noteKo.exampleTr: 이 고기는 사람이 먹기에 적합하지 않다.
noteKo.meaning: 먹거나 쓰는 행위 또는 그 양.
noteKo.usage: fit for human consumption은 먹기에 적합한. 동사는 consume.

consumption.zh: 食用；消耗（fit for consumption：適合食用）

contending.en: arguing or saying firmly that something is true
contending.ex: Critics are contending that the tax is unfair.

contracts.ex: The players signed new contracts yesterday.

cooperate.ex: Neighbours cooperate to keep the street clean.

cosmetic.en: about how something looks, not how good it is
cosmetic.ex: The car only has cosmetic damage.

could.en: might possibly; would be able to

cover.ex: The order will cover our needs for a month.
cover.zh: 涵蓋；包含（合約所需數量）

crops.en: (crop up) appears or happens, often unexpectedly
crops.ex: Problems often crop up in the first week.

day.en: a period of 24 hours; a special day
day.ex: Saturday is my favourite day of the week.
day.zh: 日；天（World Food Day：世界糧食日）

declaration.en: an official written statement or promise
declaration.ex: The leaders signed a declaration on clean energy.

donating.ex: Donating old clothes helps people in need.

early.ex: Early visitors got the best seats.

easy.ex: This recipe is quick and easy.

eaten.en: past participle of eat; taken as food
eaten.ex: The cake was eaten in five minutes.

edible.en: safe and good enough to eat
edible.ex: Some wild mushrooms are edible, but many are not.

example.en: The skin of this fruit is edible.

note.meaning: 可以安全食用的；本文指被丟棄但其實還能吃的食物。
note.usage: 多作形容詞放在名詞前或 be 動詞後；反義詞是 inedible。比 eatable 更正式。

noteEn.meaning: safe and good enough to eat.
noteEn.usage: It is an adjective; the opposite is inedible.

noteEs.exampleTr: La piel de esta fruta es comestible.
noteEs.meaning: que se puede comer sin peligro.
noteEs.usage: Es adjetivo; lo contrario es inedible. Más formal que eatable.

noteHi.exampleTr: इस फल का छिलका खाने योग्य है।
noteHi.meaning: जिसे सुरक्षित रूप से खाया जा सके।
noteHi.usage: विशेषण है; विलोम inedible है। eatable से अधिक औपचारिक।

noteJa.exampleTr: この果物の皮は食べられる。
noteJa.usage: 形容詞。反対語は inedible。eatable より改まった語。

noteKo.exampleTr: 이 과일의 껍질은 먹을 수 있다.
noteKo.usage: 형용사이며 반의어는 inedible. eatable보다 격식 있는 말.

encourages.en: tries to make someone do something
encourages.ex: The app encourages people to walk more.

encouraging.en: making others want to do something
encouraging.ex: Teachers keep encouraging students to read more.

end.en: (end up) finally be in a situation you did not plan
end.ex: We got lost and ended up in the wrong town.
end.ja: 結局〜することになる（end up）

environment.en: the natural world of land, air and water

equivalent.ex: Ten euros is equivalent to about eleven dollars.

estimates.ex: The report estimates that prices will rise.

excess.ex: Cut off any excess fat from the meat.

extra.ex: We made extra soup for the neighbours.

factories.ex: Many factories closed during the crisis.

fail.en: to not succeed in doing something
fail.ex: Some apples fail to reach the shops.

fails.en: does not succeed in doing something
fails.ex: If the plan fails, we will try again.

falls.en: (falls foul of) fails to meet a rule or standard
falls.ex: The advert fell foul of the new rules.
falls.hi: (नियम पर) खरा न उतरना (fall foul of)
falls.zh: fall foul of：違反；不符合（規定）

far.ex: This bike is far lighter than my old one.

farmers.en: people who own or run farms

figure.ex: The official figure is much higher.

first.ex: This is the first time I have visited Japan.

fit.ex: The water is not fit to drink.
fit.zh: 適合的（fit for consumption：適合食用）

food.ex: We throw away too much food.

foodcloud.ja: フードクラウド（アイルランドの慈善団体）
foodcloud.zh: FoodCloud（愛爾蘭食物分享慈善機構）

for.en: used to say who something is meant for

foul.en: (fall foul of) break a rule or fail a standard
foul.ex: The shop fell foul of safety laws.

framing.en: presenting an idea in a particular way
framing.ex: He is framing the plan as a way to save money.

from.en: used to show where something starts; stop from = prevent

fruit.en: food that grows on plants, like apples
fruit.ex: She eats fruit with her breakfast.

gave.ex: The teacher gave out the exam papers.

generated.ex: Wind farms generated a lot of power last year.

generates.ex: The festival generates a lot of rubbish.

give.ex: Please give this book to your brother.

go.en: (go to waste) be wasted, not used
go.ex: Don't let this lovely cake go to waste.

good.en: of good quality; still fine to use or eat
good.ex: This bread is still good to eat.

government.en: the group that runs a country

government-backed.ex: A government-backed loan helped the farm.

government-endorsed.ex: The school uses a government-endorsed reading list.

government-supported.en: helped and backed by the government
government-supported.ex: The government-supported scheme helps young farmers.

grow.en: to plant and look after crops
grow.ex: They grow potatoes and carrots in the garden.

growers.en: people who grow fruit or vegetables
growers.ex: Local growers sell at the market.

harvest.ex: They harvest the grapes in September.

have.en: to own or hold; to be in a situation
have.ja: 持つ；〜しなければならない

head.ex: She is the head of the science department.
head.zh: 負責人；主管（head of policy：政策主管）

heavyweights.en: very large or important companies or people
heavyweights.ex: Tech heavyweights met to discuss the new law.

held.ex: The wedding was held in a small church.

highlighted.ex: The report highlighted the need for more teachers.

inaugural.en: first in a series of events
inaugural.ex: The inaugural race was held in 1990.

example.en: The inaugural festival attracted ten thousand visitors.
example.zh: 首屆音樂節吸引了一萬名遊客。

note.meaning: 首屆的、第一次舉辦的；本文指第一屆食物分享高峰會。
note.usage: 只放在名詞前，常搭配 event、summit、season 等；也可指就職的（inaugural speech）。

noteEn.meaning: first in a series of events.
noteEn.usage: Use it only before a noun, e.g. inaugural summit.

noteEs.exampleTr: El festival inaugural atrajo a diez mil visitantes.
noteEs.meaning: primero de una serie de eventos.
noteEs.usage: Va delante del sustantivo (inaugural summit); también significa de investidura.

noteHi.exampleTr: पहले उत्सव में दस हज़ार लोग आए।
noteHi.usage: केवल संज्ञा से पहले आता है, जैसे inaugural summit; उद्घाटन भाषण के लिए भी।

noteJa.exampleTr: 第1回のフェスティバルには1万人が訪れた。
noteJa.meaning: 第1回の；初めて開かれる。
noteJa.usage: 名詞の前だけで使う（inaugural summit）。就任の意味もある。

noteKo.exampleTr: 첫 번째 축제에는 만 명이 방문했다.
noteKo.usage: 명사 앞에서만 쓴다(inaugural summit). 취임의 뜻도 있다.

include.en: have as a part or member
include.ex: The team includes two new players.

initiative.en: a new plan to solve a problem
initiative.ex: The initiative aims to plant a million trees.

instance.ex: There are many instances of kindness in the story.

intend.ex: We intend to finish by Friday.

intends.en: plans or means to do something
intends.ex: The school intends to hire more teachers.
intends.ja: 〜するつもりだ；予定している

issue.ex: Housing is a major issue for young people.

just.ex: Just over half the class passed.

land.ex: The farmer owns a lot of land near the river.

large.ex: Large cities often have traffic problems.

last.en: the one before this one (e.g. last year)
last.ex: We went to Japan last summer.

launch.en: the start or first public showing of a plan
launch.ex: The launch of the new app is next week.

launched.en: started or made public for the first time
launched.ex: The new website was launched in May.
launched.ja: 発表された；開始された

left.en: remaining after the rest is used or gone
left.ex: There is some pizza left over from last night.
left.zh: 剩下（left over：剩餘；be left with：只剩下）

linking.ex: A new bus line is linking the two towns.

links.ex: This road links the village to the city.

lot.en: a lot of: a large amount of
lot.ex: She drinks a lot of coffee.

maintains.ex: She maintains that she was at home all night.
maintains.hi: कायम रखता है; दावा करता है

major.ex: The city is planning a major new park.

make.ex: This bag of rice will make ten meals.

manufacturers.en: companies that make goods in large numbers
manufacturers.ex: Car manufacturers are making more electric models.

may.ja: …かもしれない；…することがある

meals.ex: We eat three meals a day.

meet.ex: The new cars meet strict safety rules.

meeting.en: an event where people gather to talk

mere.ex: The tickets sold out in a mere ten minutes.

minister.en: a senior member of a government who heads a department
minister.ex: The minister answered questions from reporters.

ministers.ex: The ministers met to discuss the budget.

month.en: one of the 12 parts of a year
month.ex: I visit my parents once a month.

month's.ex: Next month's concert is already sold out.

more.en: a larger amount or number (more than)

much.zh: 許多；大部分（much of：…的很多）

musgrave.ja: マスグレイブ（アイルランドの食品小売企業）

need.ex: Children need fresh food to grow.

networks.en: groups of people or organisations that work together
networks.ex: The charity has a network of volunteers.

nevertheless.ex: It was raining; nevertheless, we went out.

new.ex: The city opened a new library.

no.zh: 沒有（no choice / no alternative：別無選擇）

often.ex: We often eat lunch in the park.

organisation.en: a group such as a charity or company
organisation.ex: She works for a charity organisation.

other.ex: She moved to another city to find other work.

out.ex: They handed out free bottles of water.

overproduce.en: to make or grow more than is needed
overproduce.ex: Factories sometimes overproduce and must cut prices.

part.en: a piece or section of something larger
part.ex: This part of the city is very quiet.

people.ex: Many people visit the market on Sundays.

per.ex: The ticket costs ten euro per person.

perfectly.ex: The old bike still works perfectly.

place.ex: The concert will take place in the park.

plan.en: a set of actions decided on to achieve something
plan.ex: The city has a plan to build more parks.

plans.ex: She plans to visit her aunt next week.

pledge.ex: The town made a pledge to plant more trees.

plough.en: to turn over soil with a farm machine
plough.ex: The farmer will plough the field in spring.

ploughing.en: turning over soil with a farm machine
ploughing.ex: He spent the morning ploughing the field.

policy.en: a set of plans and ideas of an organisation
policy.ex: The new housing policy starts in May.

present.en: to show formally to a group
present.ex: Each student will present a project to the class.

preserving.en: saving something so it is not lost

produce.en: to grow or make; (n.) fruit and vegetables

producers.en: people who make or grow things
producers.ex: Ireland is a big producer of beef.

produces.ex: This farm produces milk and cheese.

promote.en: to help something become known or used
promote.ex: The town wants to promote cycling.

proportion.ex: A large proportion of students live nearby.

public.en: run by the state for everyone
public.ex: The library is a public building.

pull.en: (pull together) work together as a team
pull.ex: If we all pull together, we can finish today.

recourse.en: something you can use or turn to for help
recourse.ex: Without savings, they had no recourse but to borrow.

example.en: With the shop closed, we had no recourse but to wait.
example.zh: 商店關門了，我們只能等待。

note.meaning: 在困難時可以依靠或求助的辦法。
note.usage: 常用 have no/little recourse but to do（除了…別無他法）或 without recourse to。

noteEn.meaning: something you can turn to for help in a problem.
noteEn.usage: Often in 'have no recourse but to' = have no other choice.

noteEs.exampleTr: Con la tienda cerrada, no tuvimos más remedio que esperar.
noteEs.meaning: opción a la que se puede recurrir en un problema.
noteEs.usage: Común en have no recourse but to (no tener más remedio que).

noteHi.exampleTr: दुकान बंद होने पर हमारे पास इंतज़ार के सिवा कोई उपाय नहीं था।
noteHi.usage: have no recourse but to (इसके सिवा कोई उपाय नहीं) में आम।

noteJa.exampleTr: 店が閉まっていたので、待つしかなかった。
noteJa.meaning: 困った時に頼れる手段。
noteJa.usage: have no recourse but to（〜するしかない）の形が多い。

noteKo.exampleTr: 가게가 닫혀서 우리는 기다릴 수밖에 없었다.
noteKo.meaning: 어려울 때 의지할 수 있는 방법.
noteKo.usage: have no recourse but to(~할 수밖에 없다) 형태로 자주 쓴다.

redistributed.en: shared out again to other people
redistributed.ex: The unused tickets were redistributed to students.

example.en: The app helps cafés redistribute unsold food to students.
example.zh: 這個應用程式幫助咖啡店把沒賣完的食物轉送給學生。

note.meaning: 把東西重新分配給其他人；本文指把多餘食物轉送給需要的人。
note.usage: 常用 redistribute A to B；re- 表示「再」，distribute 是「分發」。名詞為 redistribution。

noteEn.meaning: to share something out again to different people.
noteEn.usage: Use redistribute A to B; the noun is redistribution.

noteEs.exampleTr: La aplicación ayuda a las cafeterías a redistribuir la comida no vendida entre estudiantes.
noteEs.meaning: repartir algo de nuevo entre otras personas.
noteEs.usage: Se usa redistribute A to B; el sustantivo es redistribution.

noteHi.exampleTr: यह ऐप कैफ़े को बिना बिका खाना छात्रों में बाँटने में मदद करता है।
noteHi.meaning: चीज़ों को फिर से दूसरों में बाँटना।
noteHi.usage: redistribute A to B के रूप में प्रयोग होता है; संज्ञा redistribution है।

noteJa.exampleTr: そのアプリはカフェが売れ残った食品を学生に再分配するのを助ける。
noteJa.meaning: 物を他の人々に配り直すこと。
noteJa.usage: redistribute A to B の形で使う。名詞は redistribution。

noteKo.exampleTr: 그 앱은 카페가 팔리지 않은 음식을 학생들에게 재분배하도록 돕는다.
noteKo.meaning: 물건을 다른 사람들에게 다시 나누어 주다.
noteKo.usage: redistribute A to B 형태로 쓴다. 명사는 redistribution.

redistributing.en: sharing out again to other people
redistributing.ex: The club is redistributing old sports kits.

example.en: The app helps cafés redistribute unsold food to students.
example.zh: 這個應用程式幫助咖啡店把沒賣完的食物轉送給學生。

note.meaning: 把東西重新分配給其他人；本文指把多餘食物轉送給需要的人。
note.usage: 常用 redistribute A to B；re- 表示「再」，distribute 是「分發」。名詞為 redistribution。

noteEn.meaning: to share something out again to different people.
noteEn.usage: Use redistribute A to B; the noun is redistribution.

noteEs.exampleTr: La aplicación ayuda a las cafeterías a redistribuir la comida no vendida entre estudiantes.
noteEs.meaning: repartir algo de nuevo entre otras personas.
noteEs.usage: Se usa redistribute A to B; el sustantivo es redistribution.

noteHi.exampleTr: यह ऐप कैफ़े को बिना बिका खाना छात्रों में बाँटने में मदद करता है।
noteHi.meaning: चीज़ों को फिर से दूसरों में बाँटना।
noteHi.usage: redistribute A to B के रूप में प्रयोग होता है; संज्ञा redistribution है।

noteJa.exampleTr: そのアプリはカフェが売れ残った食品を学生に再分配するのを助ける。
noteJa.meaning: 物を他の人々に配り直すこと。
noteJa.usage: redistribute A to B の形で使う。名詞は redistribution。

paragraphs: Ireland throws away a lot of food. Every year, about 708,000 tonnes of food become waste. Not all of it can be eaten, but much of it can.
On Friday, a new plan started in Dublin. It asks shops, farmers and charities to work together. They should give extra food to people who need it.
Saving only 3 per cent of extra food could make 50 million meals a year. Last year, the charity FoodCloud saved over 4,000 tonnes of food. That is about 10 million meals.
Big shops like Aldi, Lidl and Tesco signed the plan. The Government will show it at a world climate meeting next month.
Ireland produces about 708,000 tonnes of food waste every year, according to the charity FoodCloud. Not all of this food can be eaten, but a large part of it could be shared with people who need it.

A new plan, supported by the Government, was launched in Dublin on Friday, which was World Food Day. It asks food businesses, farmers, charities and public bodies to work together to stop good food from being thrown away. It says that saving just 3 per cent of surplus food could provide 50 million meals a year.

Farmers sometimes grow more than their contracts need, or their fruit and vegetables are the wrong size or shape for buyers. Often they have no choice but to plough the extra food back into the soil. Restaurants and factories also have food left over.

Last year, FoodCloud gave out more than 4,000 tonnes of food, or about 10 million meals. Companies including Aldi, Lidl, Tesco and Musgrave were among the first to sign up. The Government plans to present the plan at the COP31 climate summit next month.

Ireland generates around 708,000 tonnes of food waste every year, and a significant share of it is perfectly edible, according to the charity FoodCloud. Its head of policy, Angela Ruttledge, says far more of this surplus should be redistributed.

Her comments came as a Government-backed declaration on sharing and redistributing surplus food was launched at the first Food Sharing Summit in Dublin on Friday, which coincided with World Food Day. The initiative calls on food businesses, farmers, charities and public agencies to cooperate, claiming that rescuing just 3 per cent of surplus food could supply 50 million meals annually.

Surplus arises at many stages. Farmers may harvest more than their contracts cover, or produce that fails to meet buyers' size and shape requirements, and they often end up ploughing it back into the land. Manufacturers and restaurants also have excess stock.

FoodCloud redistributed more than 4,000 tonnes last year, the equivalent of 10 million meals. Early signatories include Aldi, Lidl, Tesco, Musgrave and Ballymaloe. Environment Minister Darragh O'Brien said treating surplus food as a resource would support climate action and food security, and the Government intends to promote the declaration at the COP31 climate summit next month.

A staggering 708,000 tonnes of food go to waste in Ireland each year, and a considerable proportion of it is fit for consumption, according to FoodCloud, the charity that links producers with people in need.

The figure was highlighted as a Government-endorsed declaration on surplus food sharing was unveiled at the inaugural Food Sharing Summit in Dublin, held on World Food Day. The pledge urges food businesses, growers, charities and state agencies to pull together, contending that salvaging a mere 3 per cent of surplus could yield 50 million meals a year.

Excess food crops up throughout the supply chain. Growers frequently overproduce relative to their contracts or are left with produce that falls foul of buyers' cosmetic standards, and many have little recourse but to plough it back into the soil. FoodCloud's Angela Ruttledge argues that linking farmers to redistribution networks must become viable, and that donating surplus should be an easy choice for manufacturers and restaurants.

Last year the charity rescued more than 4,000 tonnes, equivalent to 10 million meals. Retail heavyweights such as Aldi, Lidl, Tesco and Musgrave were among the first to sign up, and ministers intend to champion the initiative at next month's COP31 climate summit, framing surplus food as a resource rather than refuse.

In such circumstances, they frequently have no alternative but to return it to the soil. Similarly, manufacturers and restaurants accumulate excess food.
